title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board of Trustees met Tuesday evening at the Village Hall.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order and informed those gathered that he wanted to keep the meeting short.  He announced that Clay City Engineer Mike Bridges had passed away.  Bridges, the owner of Charleston Engineering in Olney, has served numerous cities and villages in our area for many decades.  His services were utilized for Flora’s Pickle Ball Courts and Louisville’s Pavillion on the Courthouse Square and numerous other projects including the construction of new roads and the annual oiling and chipping of streets around Clay County and beyond.  Consensus of the Clay City Board and countless others is that he will be deeply missed, and condolences are offered to his family.

Trustees quickly approved the past meeting minutes and the bills.  A short time later, Attorney Barry Bright stated that the board needed to discuss and act on the backlog of audio tapes from past closed meeting sessions dating back many years ago.  Bright pointed out that the board can vote to destroy the recordings as long as the written closed session minutes are retained.  Trustee Sue Lindeman pointed out that there was one meeting from February 1, 2022, that was not included in the closed meeting minutes.  Clerk Shannon Hall quickly located the closed minutes from that date, and the board will likely act at the April meeting.  Bright said he will author the resolution, but before it is enacted, the board will meet in closed session to straighten out the so-called missing minutes and then return to open session  to formally approve the resolution.

The agenda listed a representative of Leymone Hardcastle CPA’s would present the annual village audit.  The rep was not able to attend, and the item was tabled until the April meeting.

Utility Superintendent Sean Sullens briefly identified his discussion with professionals about the operation of the village sewer plant and the steps they are taking to ensure its continued safe operation.

Clerk Shannon Hall states no action was needed concerning the village’s monthly cash balance and transfer report.  Hall said Clay City Post Prom is requesting $100 and members quickly approved the Donation.  There was also a request for the village to purchase an ad in the Clay City High School Yearbook.  Trustees voted to once again purchase a $35 ad.  Shannon Hall also asked the board to approve the Townwide Cleanup dates and renting a dumpster.  Members approved the spring date of April 17-May3 and for fall September 18-October 4.  The dumpster will have controlled access for Clay City residents who will need to contact the village hall prior to use.

Trustee Jim Duff reminded fellow members that they had appropriated around $2,500 to purchase concrete jersey barriers that are used on highways and to protect areas from vehicle mishaps and such.  Duff said a local farmer has several of the barriers for sale and he thought it would be a good idea for the village to purchase several of them.  Consensus was for the village to purchase 30 of them for $70 each with the funds that were already earmarked for that purpose.

The Cemetery Committee reminds everyone that all ground flowers at the Clay City Cemetery need to be removed by April 1st.  And will all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: MITIGATION PLANNING COMMITTEE MEETING
full_story:
The Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee will hold its first meeting on Wednesday, March 18th, at 1:00 PM.  The meeting will be at the Clay County Health Department and is open to the public.

Clay County will update its hazard mitigation plan to reduce the damages caused by severe weather such as thunderstorms, floods, snow and ice storms, and tornados, among other events.  This plan and the process to update it will be funded through a grant from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).

“The Plan describes the natural hazard events that have impacted the County and identifies activities and projects to reduce the risk to our residents and infrastructure,” said Steve Lewis, Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency Coordinator.  “By having an updated hazard mitigation plan, the County and its participating jurisdictions will remain eligible for federal funds to carry out these projects and activities,” he added.

The Planning Committee includes representatives from the County, their municipalities, townships, school districts, fire protection districts, and healthcare services, as well as technical partners and other stakeholders.  Meetings of this committee will be conducted over the next year as working sessions so that any interested residents can attend and ask questions.  The purpose of these working sessions is to gather and discuss information that will be used to update the Plan.

Lewis added, “This mitigation plan is different from our County’s emergency response plan because it focuses on ways to reduce and prevent damages before they occur.”

title: CHICKEN DINNER
full_story:
The Flora Wolfpack Football Boosters club will be having a chicken dinner fundraiser on Sunday, March 22nd at Floyd Henson JR. High.

title: FAFSA NIGHT
full_story:
Olney Central College is hosting a FAFSA Completion Night from 3 to 6 pm on Tuesday, March 24th in Room 205 on the second floor of Dr. Kent L. Wattleworth Hall.

OCC Financial Aid experts will be available to answer questions and assist students and parents in Filing the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA).  Those attending should bring their FSA ID and 2024 tax returns to simplify the process.

While the event is open to everyone, the OCC Financial Aid staff especially encourages high school seniors who have not yet completed the FAFSA to attend, as it is required by the state for high school graduation.

For more information or if you have questions about the FAFSA, visit www.iecc.edu/financial, or contact OCC Financial Aid at 618-395-7777, ext. 2017.

title: FRIENDS OF THE LIBRARY SPRING BOOK SALE
full_story:
The Friends of the Flora Public Library Spring Book Sale will be held on Saturday, April 11th at the Flora Public Library.  The sale will be from 8:00 am to 3:00 pm, in the library community room.  Books, DVD’s and CD’s will be .25 each and magazines will be priced at .10 each or 12 for $1.

Anyone wishing to contribute books, magazines, DVDs, or CDs to the book sale can bring them to the east door of the Flora Public Library during regular library hours.  The Flora Public Library is open Monday – Thursday 1:00 – 8:00 pm, Friday 10:00 am – 6:00 pm and Saturday 10:00 am – 3:00 pm.

The last day to make donations to the spring book sale is April the 6th.

title: MAKERS MADNESS CONTEST
full_story:
The 2026 “Makers Madness” contest is now taking nominations for the Coolest Thing Made in Illinois.  Nominations will be accepted through Sunday at https://makersmadnessil.com/.  The bracket-style tournament is hosted every spring by the Illinois Manufacturer’s Association.

Last year the Rain Light Sensor from Hella in Flora made the top 16 and the Aerial Firefighting Helicopter Refill Pump made by MTH pumps in Plano was crowned the winner.  The drone to clean oil and fuel spills from water in hard-to-reach places like piers and around ships made by Elastec in Carmi made it into the quarter finals.

Those items nominated will be whittled down to the top 16 and voting will begin on March 10th.  The second round of voting for the Top 8 will begin on March 31st with the items receiving the top 4 votes, going head-to-head beginning on April 7th.  With the winner announced on April 15th.  Last year over 250 items were nominated for the top prize.

title: FISHING LICENSES
full_story:
Illinois fishing licenses, among the most affordable in the nation; are now on sale for the 2026 season.  Illinois fishing licenses and stamps for 2026 are available for purchase online and at department-authorized vendors.

A standard, non-discounted resident fishing license costs $15.  Licenses for the 2025 season remain valid through March 31.  Anglers 16 and older must have a valid fishing license in Illinois.  Exemptions apply to active-duty military personnel and people with disabilities.

When anglers purchase a fishing license, they support conservation, education and economic activity across the state.  Purchases help enhance outdoor recreation opportunities statewide and ensure future generations can enjoy Illinois’ aquatic resources.

“Quality fishing opportunities depend on the support of anglers, and that starts with buying a fishing license,” said Mike McClelland, chief of fisheries for the Illinois Department of Natural Resources.  “When anglers buy a license, they help support sport fishing, hatcheries and habitat improvements for people across Illinois, now and in the future.”

IDNR’s Division of Fisheries is funded primarily through the sale of fishing licenses and associated stamps.  Key fisheries programs supported by license and stamp sales include research, fisheries management, hatchery operations, invasive species prevention, outdoor education and other initiatives.

Additional support comes from the Sport Fish Restoration Program of 1950, administered by the US Fish and Wildlife Service.  The program distributes funding to states through federal excise taxes on fishing equipment, motorboat fuel and related outdoor accessories.  Funding allocations are based on land area and each state’s fishing license sales.

For more information about fishing in Illinois visit ifishillinois.org.  To review license and stamp fees, visit the IDNR website.  The current Illinois fishing regulations guide is also available online.
